mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5%, it indicates a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the cases when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the cases when UNRATE is below 5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in real GDP (GDPC1) indicates strong economic activity, which increases corporate revenues and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the cases when GDPC1 growth is positive, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals increased economic output, which supports equity valuations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the cases when INDPRO increases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 5%, it indicates a tight labor market and high borrowing costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the cases when FEDFUNDS > 4% and UNRATE < 5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, an increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) leads to higher borrowing costs and reduced consumer and business spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the cases during a monetary tightening cycle, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real estate investment (RSAFS) indicates strong housing market activity, which supports economic growth and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the cases when RSAFS increases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the cases when PAYEMS increases, the hypothesis is rejected.
